clue.text: Decency in art form — odd?

parts.note: Deco, short for Art Deco, is a style of decorative art
rum is an old British word for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A critic wonders whether there is any decency in a strange kind of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly behaviour, which is a synonym for decency.

clue.text: New Orleans style up river

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: trad, short for traditional jazz, is the New Orleans style

explanation.surface: A jazz style from New Orleans travels upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a river in Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: S for Stockholm

definitions.meaning: S is the capital, the first and uppercase letter, of the word Sweden
Stockholm is the chief city and seat of government of Sweden

explanation.walkthrough: Capital means both an initial capital letter and a chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the initial letter of the country's name and its main city.

clue.text: Trabant once seen in Cleveland?

definitions.meaning: the Trabant was an East German car
A seaside town in the former English county of Cleveland

explanation.walkthrough: Cleveland is not the US city but a former county in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar is a Teesside town, and a Trabant was a car from the communist, or red, bloc.

clue.text: Motorway madness is an illusion

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I
rage is a fit of madness

explanation.surface: Road rage on the motorway is a form of delusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north; the figure 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert.

clue.text: Authorise soldiers to return holding prisoner

indicators.note: holding means the soldiers' letters wrap round the prisoner
to return tells us the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
POW is the usual abbreviation for prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Troops are ordered back to base while keeping a captive in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps, so its members are soldiers; 'to return' and 'holding' work on it in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority, the same as to authorise them.

clue.text: Tesco ragout goes down well in Paris

annotationWithheld.clue: Tesco ragout goes down well in Paris

clue.text: Water found in some pesticide

indicators.note: found in means the water goes inside the next piece

parts.note: a part is some of something
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: Traces of water turn up in a crop spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraquat is a highly toxic weedkiller, a kind of pesticide.

clue.text: Beyond the pale?

parts.note: read literally, beyond pale means paler still, past white itself

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond the pale' normally means unacceptable; here pale is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means spotless or morally pure, literally paler than the palest colour.

clue.text: Correct gear for drill order

parts.note: right means correct
dress means clothing or gear

explanation.surface: The proper kit for military parade.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Right dress' is a parade-ground command for soldiers to line up.

clue.text: Swift pounce involving copper

indicators.note: involving means the raid takes the copper inside it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden swoop or pounce on a target
P stands for penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A quick swoop by the police that pulls in a constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests CU or a policeman; here it is a copper coin, the penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are straightforward synonyms meaning very fast.

clue.text: Like an angel with a book or disc

definitions.text: Like an angel with a book
definitions.meaning: the ... angel is said to write down every deed in a heavenly book
a disc such as a record or CD holds a piece of captured sound

explanation.walkthrough: The recording angel of tradition keeps a book of everyone's good and bad deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a sound recording, and the recording angel keeps a written record in a book.

clue.text: Unusual petition generating street anger (queer street)

annotationWithheld.clue: Unusual petition generating street anger (queer street)

clue.text: Students' wine bar set up in post-war city

definitions.text: Students' wine bar set up in post-war city

parts.words: Students' wine bar set up in post-war city
parts.note: the bar is not a drinking place but a barrier, set up as in erected across a divided city after the war

explanation.walkthrough: Bar here means barrier; the student wine bar is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrier built across Berlin in 1961 divided the city in the post-war years.

clue.text: She does a turn for orchestra lacking leader

indicators.note: does a turn means the remaining letters are read backwards
lacking leader means the orchestra's first letter is dropped

parts.note: the Hallé is a famous Manchester orchestra

explanation.surface: A soloist performs a number for an orchestra whose conductor is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking leader' takes H off HALLE, leaving ALLE, and 'does a turn' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a woman's given name, so it can stand for 'she'.

clue.text: Signed minor firm with works nearing completion

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: nearing completion means the word is not quite finished, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A young person signed up by a company whose building project is almost done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signed minor' looks like an underage contract; in matrix algebra a cofactor is a minor given a plus or minus sign.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a cofactor is a matrix minor multiplied by plus or minus one, literally a signed minor.

clue.text: Where one finds change at the centre of Dunstable

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are rearranged
at the centre of means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A traveller looks for coins in the middle of a Bedfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the centre of' gives UNSTABL from Dunstable, and 'change' rearranges it to STANBUL. Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is a city, so it answers the question where.

clue.text: It's hard to join actors' club

parts.note: the cast is the group of actors in a show
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Getting into a theatrical society proves difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron describes something hard, rigid or unbreakable.

clue.text: Morning, they say, begins when it's over

definitions.text: Morning, they say, begins when it's over

parts.words: Morning, they say, begins when it's over
parts.note: morning sounds like mourning, and mourning starts when a person's time alive has run out

explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals that morning should be heard as mourning, which begins at a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifespan is the length of a life, and mourning starts at its end.

clue.text: Drink for a singer …

definitions.meaning: A well-known British brand of beer
a male singer with the lowest voice

explanation.walkthrough: Bass is a British pale ale brewed in Burton upon Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass names both a brand of English ale and the lowest male singing voice.

clue.text: CO's speech in a nutshell

indicators.note: speech means the word is heard as spoken

parts.note: a commanding officer, CO, is often a colonel

explanation.surface: The commanding officer gives a brief summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a nutshell' looks like 'briefly' but means literally what lies inside a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the edible part found inside a nut's shell.

clue.text: Order of the Garter for culinary service

indicators.note: order means arrangement, so the word's letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A knightly honour awarded for kitchen work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Garter is Britain's senior order of knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a kitchen tool that serves for shredding cheese or vegetables.

clue.text: … or fresh piece by a politician

parts.note: fresh means new
a castle is a chess piece, also called a rook
Gordon Brown was a British Labour Chancellor and Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A new chessman placed beside a Westminster figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 18 across, so 'Drink' there defines this answer too. Newcastle Brown is a strong brown ale from north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle Brown is a bottled brown ale, so it is a drink, as the linked 18 across says.

clue.text: Where there's no right to wander, don't!

indicators.note: where there's no means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to stray is to wander

explanation.surface: A sign warns walkers off land with no public right of way.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'right to roam' lets walkers cross some private land; here there is none.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay is the command 'don't wander off', as said to a dog.

clue.text: Man introducing Debra could be a star

indicators.note: introducing means the man's name takes other letters inside it

parts.note: Alan is a man's name

indicators.note: could be signals that the name Debra may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man introduces a woman called Debra, who might become a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the woman's name, and 'introducing' sets the result inside the man's name; 'star' is not a celebrity but the bright star in Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red giant star in the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: Blemish denied by Londoner

definitions.meaning: a blemish is a stain or mark of corruption
a Cockney might deny something with '..., short for it ain't

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney (working-class London) speech 'tain't means 'it isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or a moral stain, a blemish.

clue.text: Fat proceeds from loan with nothing to return

indicators.note: proceeds from suggests the letters of loan are worked into a new arrangement
to return means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Profits come from a loan that you never need to repay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds from' rearranges LOAN as LANO; 'to return' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy fat taken from sheep's wool, used in creams.

clue.text: Nearly caught involved in crime

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone was almost arrested after taking part in an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes up NEARLY and C to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, a particular crime.
